newsitem.title: GERMANY: Goldhagen wins German prize for Holocaust book.
newsitem.headline: Goldhagen wins German prize for Holocaust book.

text.p: American historian Daniel Goldhagen was honoured by a German magazine on Tuesday for his best-selling book about the attitudes of ordinary Germans during the Holocaust which stirred heated national debate.

The Magazine for German and International Politics in Bonn said it picked Goldhagen for its 1997 Democracy Award because his book, "Hitler's Willing Executioners", had given the German public fresh impetus to discuss the Holocaust.

Goldhagen, a Harvard university sociologist, prompted a ferocious debate last year with his book, published first in English and later in German. It argued that most Germans were willing accomplices of Hitler because of a deep-seated tradition of German anti-Semitism.

"Because of the urgency and moral force of his work, Goldhagen has given the German public consciousness significant new impulses in this crucial period of the transition from the Bonn republic to the Berlin republic," the magazine said in announcing the 10,000-mark ($6,400) award.

The magazine's Democracy Prize, due to be officially presented in Bonn on March 10, was last awarded in 1990, to the representatives of the democratic movement of the former East Germany. ($1=1.5653 Mark)
